endorsements.quote: Laboratory medicine should actively partner with clinical specialties, bioinformatics, data science, and public health to co-develop, validate, and implement predictive tools, ensuring their effective integration into holistic care pathways for prevention, diagnosis, and management ( 51 ).

A multifaceted strategy is required: technically, implementing phased real-world validation and developing industry standards for data and algorithms ( 69 , 70 ); ethically, promoting transparent communication and shared decision-making ( 71 ); and systemically, aligning payment models with preventive care and supporting workforce development through education and role redesign ( 72 ).

unlisted_practices: Train laboratory professionals and clinicians in data literacy, risk communication, critical evaluation of predictive models, and ethical awareness.
Develop uniform protocols for data collection, formatting, and exchange to standardize data used in predictive models.
Establish clear protocols for interpretation and clinical response before clinical use of predictive models.
Align reimbursement and payment models with preventive risk assessment to support adoption.
Develop tailored, context-sensitive implementation strategies for resource-limited settings rather than a uniform global approach.
Provide clear legal and regulatory guidance on accountability for decisions based on predictive outputs.
Use careful risk communication frameworks when communicating probabilistic risk to patients.

screen.reason: This is a perspective article discussing the conceptual paradigm shift, implementation pathways, and ethical/system challenges of integrating AI and predictive systems into laboratory medicine.
